title: Is Your Neighborhood Safe? Place-based Stigma in Large Language Models' Urban Safety Judgments
abstract: arXiv:2608.26188v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to inform safety decisions in cities, such as where it is safe to walk, rent, or travel. We ask whether such judgments track measured risk or the patterns attached to an urban neighborhood's name. We probe seven instruct-tuned models under three conditions that dissociate name from geography: coordinates-only, name-only, and name+coordinates, across 186 neighborhoods in Los Angeles and Chicago, joined to violent crime and American Community Survey data. First, ratings are nearly flat under coordinates for six of seven models, while names carry most between neighborhood variation and are moderately calibrated to violent crime; only at frontier scale does the coordinate channel show appreciable variation. Second, names lower safety ratings more for neighborhoods with higher shares of the locally dominant marginalized group (percent Black in Chicago, percent Hispanic in Los Angeles), and this name

translated_title: 你的社区安全吗？大型语言模型城市安全判断中的地点污名化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26188v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大型语言模型越来越多地被用于为城市安全决策提供信息，例如哪些地方适合步行、租房或旅行。我们探讨这类判断是否追踪实测风险，还是追踪城市社区名称所附带的模式。我们在三种条件下探究了七个指令调优模型，这些条件将名称与地理分离：仅坐标、仅名称和名称+坐标，覆盖洛杉矶和芝加哥的186个社区，并结合暴力犯罪和美国社区调查数据。首先，在仅坐标条件下，七个模型中有六个的评分几乎持平，而名称承载了社区间的大部分差异，并与暴力犯罪中度校准；只有在前沿规模下，坐标通道才显示出显著变化。其次，名称对当地主导边缘化群体（芝加哥的黑人比例、洛杉矶的西班牙裔比例）较高社区的评分降低更多，而这种名称效应与实测犯罪风险无关。
tldr: 大型语言模型在评估城市安全时，主要依赖社区名称而非地理位置，且对边缘化群体比例高的社区存在系统性污名化偏见，与真实犯罪风险无关。
en_tdlr: Large language models' urban safety judgments are primarily driven by neighborhood names rather than geographic coordinates, exhibiting systematic stigmatization of communities with higher marginalized group shares, independent of actual crime risk.
